_what: TencentEdgeOne origin-pull (回源) IP ranges — the addresses the CDN edge connects FROM when it fetches admin.mastermind-x.com and the rest of the estate from this origin. Consumed by admin/edge_trust.py to decide whether a request's verified TCP peer is the edge (and therefore whether EO-Connecting-IP may be believed) or a direct-to-origin caller (whose every forwarded header is a forgery).
_why_empty: Because as of 2026-08-07 there is no authoritative list this infrastructure can obtain. Shipping a guess would be worse than shipping nothing: a range that is too narrow merely degrades to peer keying, but a range that is too broad lets anyone inside it forge EO-Connecting-IP and defeat the admin login lockout entirely. Prefer ADMIN_EDGE_SECRET (admin/edge_trust.py mechanism 1), which needs no list at all.

public_endpoint.observed_response: HTTP 200, Server: TencentEdgeOne, 257 bytes: a two-line deprecation notice ('This interface stopped serving on 2026-07-31 and will be officially offline on 2026-08-31') followed by the literal payload '0.0.0.0/0' and '::/0'.
public_endpoint.hazard: It answers 200 with a DEFAULT ROUTE. A refresh job that trusts the status code and skips the '#' comment lines will build a trust-everything allowlist. admin/edge_trust.py::_safe_network refuses blanket/private/non-routable entries unconditionally so this cannot land here, but any OTHER consumer (a ufw builder, a Caddy trusted_proxies generator) must make the same refusal itself.
public_endpoint.note: Tencent also documents this endpoint as mutually exclusive with the per-zone Origin Protection feature, so even before deprecation it was the coarse global list, not this zone's ACL.

successor_api.payload_field: CurrentOriginACL.EntireAddresses (live) / NextOriginACL.EntireAddresses (pending rotation; non-null means a change is queued)
successor_api.credentials: REQUIRED — Tencent Cloud SecretId/SecretKey, TC3-HMAC-SHA256. This infrastructure holds none: no TENCENT/EDGEONE/QCLOUD key exists in any /etc/macro-*.env on 146.190.142.17 and tccli is not installed (both verified 2026-08-07).
successor_api.rotation: Tencent documents ~3-6 month rotation with T-14/T-7/T-3/T-1 notifications and a 14-day confirmation window; their guidance is to poll every 3 days for a non-null NextOriginACL.

_sources.whois_is_not_a_source: The observed peers resolve to AS139341 (ACEVILLE PTE. LTD., listed in PeeringDB as 'Tencent Global CDN Platform - EdgeONE'), inside APNIC blocks such as 43.175.104.0/24. A WHOIS allocation proves who owns an address block, NOT that the block is used for origin-pull or that it holds nothing else. Those /16s also carry rentable Tencent Cloud instances, and none of the 378 observed peers has a PTR record to tell an edge node from a neighbour. Never derive this list from WHOIS.

_observed_only_do_not_trust._what: Reference evidence, NOT an allowlist. 5,179 origin-pull requests in Caddy's JSON access log over 14 days to 2026-08-07 came from 378 distinct addresses in 42 distinct /24s. Recorded so a future maintainer can sanity-check a real list against reality — an authoritative list that does not cover these is the wrong list.

_how_to_populate: Pull CurrentOriginACL.EntireAddresses from DescribeOriginACL with operator credentials and paste the CIDRs into 'ranges' below (or set ADMIN_EDGE_ORIGIN_CIDRS as a comma-separated list, which wins over this file). Entries broader than /16 (v4) or /32 (v6), and any private/loopback/link-local/multicast/reserved/unspecified block, are dropped by the loader — if a range you paste stops working, that floor is why. Re-check after every Tencent rotation notice.
